title: Signatures Trust and Recovery Polish
lede: Staff need a truthful roster surface before they send an iPad into the field: unsupported desktop actions should not mutate, and readiness should remain understandable to every reader.

stats.n: The same authenticated desktop session now shows Add on iPad before any ad-hoc mutation.
All five visible roster cards expose a label and determinate 0–100 value in the live DOM.
Before and after use the same authenticated Preview data and viewport.

sections.heading: Matched landing capture
sections.note: Source-control baseline and current local source, same authenticated Preview session, same roster data, same viewport.

pairs.title: Desktop entry and readiness
pairs.sub: The visual change is intentionally small; the stronger improvement is the mutation boundary and accessible progress contract behind it.
pairs.beforeCap: The desktop session could open Add Signature even though the next capture screen rejected non-iPad clients. Progress bars had no accessible names.
pairs.afterCap: The same session shows Add on iPad disabled. The visible roster cards retain their data while each progress bar now exposes a determinate, named value.

changesNote: The UI review covers the visible landing change; service, capture, cache, and security hardening are listed in verification and the active execution ledger.

changes.h: Add Signature crossed the device boundary too late
changes.was: A desktop operator could create an ad-hoc member and only then learn that capture required an iPad.
changes.now: The action is disabled and explained before the request is sent; Replace follows the same rule.

changes.h: Readiness looked determinate but was not announced
changes.was: The fill moved visually, but Radix received no value and the bars had no accessible name.
changes.now: The shared Progress wrapper passes its value to the semantic root and Signature call sites provide roster-specific labels.

verification: 99 focused Signatures tests pass across capture, service, route, storage, ZIP, cache, and source-contract coverage.

TypeScript, full lint, debug-prerender app build (233/233 pages), codemap verification, and git diff --check pass; the exact build:app retry remains intermittently blocked by unrelated Next page-data module errors.

Authenticated local browser proof: Add on iPad is disabled; Football's 112-member roster loads; search narrows to Danny O'Neil; desktop Replace on iPad is visible but disabled; progress bars expose aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax.
Security coverage: allowlisted UWBadgers redirects are validated before a second request; profile writes require a current READY artifact; detail history and capture bootstrap are bounded.
notes: The screenshot pair is local source proof only. The hardened source is not represented as deployed production until the normal release gate is run.
Physical iPad Safari/Apple Pencil save, interruption, rotation, and authenticated artifact delivery remain open acceptance gates under GAP-65.
Private-artifact cleanup now uses bounded concurrency and a durable state transition; late uploads self-fence when delete/reset wins the race.
